finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If argv[1] is crafted to include shell metacharacters or control operators, it could lead to command injection.
finding.assumptions: The code does not explicitly call any shell or command interpreter, but the use of fprintf with untrusted input could potentially be exploited if the file path or other parts of the code are vulnerable.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the control flow: argv[1] is only compared against the literals "up" and "down" (lines 56-61). The resulting new_brightness is computed from the current brightness and fixed increments, then clamped (lines 67-71). The value written to the file is an integer via fprintf(file, "%d", brightness) (line 43), which does not invoke a shell or execute a command. No path exists from argv[1] to the fprintf sink that could inject shell metacharacters. Therefore the claim of OS command injection is unfounded.
